Glossary

Parent Portal — A secure website where parents view their child’s grades, assignments, and teacher messages.

K-12 — Kindergarten through 12th grade.

For Parents & Guardians

Dear Texas Tech K-12 Parents and Students:

Welcome. Use the Parent Portal to see your child’s grades, assignments, and teacher messages. If you need help, call 1-800-692-6877 or Create a Case (opens in new tab).

Table of Contents

Introduction

Welcome to Texas Tech K-12! As a District Partnership Student, this page is designed to guide you through the Focus Student Portal.

If you have any questions, our Support Team may be reached via 1-800-692-6877 or by submitting a Support Ticket.

We look forward to supporting you with your Academic Journey.

Student Conduct and Academic Integrity

Texas Tech K-12 fosters a spirit of complete honesty and a high standard of integrity. An attempt to present any work you have not honestly performed as your own is regarded by Texas Tech K-12 as a serious offense leading to serious consequences.

As a part of Texas Tech University, the Texas Tech K-12 student conduct policy aligns with the university’s student policy regarding academic integrity:

“Academic dishonesty includes, but is not limited to, cheating, plagiarism, collusion, falsifying academic records, misrepresenting facts, and any act designed to give an unfair academic advantage to the student (such as, but not limited to, submission of essentially the same written assignment for two courses).”

For a full description of each of the examples above, please read Section I, Part B.1, Academic Dishonesty in the TTU Student Conduct Policy (opens in new tab).

For Counselors

Texas Tech K-12 Support can help counselors with admissions, registration, Canvas, and basic technical issues. Use our support portal to open Frequently Asked Questions or chat live: Open the Support Portal (opens in new tab). For phone help call 1-800-692-6877.

Abbreviations used on this page are defined in the Glossary / Definitions section. See Glossary / Definitions.

Final Grade Point Calculation for Graduation

If you have failed a previous transfer course, you may repeat the course for credit with Texas Tech High School.

The following designations will receive weighted credits:

Step 1: Advanced Placement or Placement

Step 2: Honors

Step 3: International Baccaluareate

Step 4: Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit

All accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses taken by a student that apply to graduation will be used to compute the GPA, excluding any approved PE Substitution (SUBPRO) credits and local credit courses.

Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will make every effort to assist students in transferring grades and credits from accredited public or private schools as allowed by Texas Education Agency (TEA) policies and Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS). An official transcript or report card will be required for credit transfer.

My Child has an Individualized Education Program (IEP) or 504 plan. May he/she enroll in your school?

Texas Tech K-12’s curriculum is developed to meet the standards of the State of Texas and the Texas Education Agency. Accommodations will be implemented based on the student’s current Individual Education Plan (IEP) or 504 documentation. The student’s IEP or 504 should reflect that Texas Tech K-12 is an appropriate placement and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

A student should obtain information regarding available disability accommodations before enrolling in a course or CBE. To request accommodations, a student must submit a current signed Individualized Education Plan (IEP) or a 504 accommodation form using our online Accommodation Request Form inside the  Focus Portal (opens in new tab).

Concurrent Diploma

This option allows students to pursue two high school diplomas—one from their local school and one from Texas Tech K-12.

Step 1: Students take a mix of online courses from Texas Tech K-12 and transfer credits from their local school.

Step 2: Students must have adequate English language skills to succeed.

Step 3: Entrance exams help assess academic and English proficiency before admission.

Step 4: Ideal for: Students looking to earn two diplomas simultaneously.

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) USE POLICY (REVISED 2025)

This policy covers any generative Artificial Intelligence tool, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer, Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

If it is determined that a student has violated final exam directions on Final Exam A or Credit By Exam Set 1, the exam will be scored as zero. The student may take Final Exam B or Credit By Exam Set 2 with the highest possible score being 70%.

The incident will be reported to Texas Tech K-12 Administration and documented in the student’s file. Continued violations of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy will result in the removal of the student from the program. Texas Tech Student Handbook (opens in new tab)

Proctorio requires 2GB of RAM. Restart your computer and make sure all other programs are closed, so they are not using memory. This should free up some RAM. Try to restart the exam. If you receive a warning about performance issues, you may need to use a different computer that has enough RAM to allow Proctorio to load the exam.

query.raw: What are the application requirements for enrolling a kindergartener?

chunks.text:
How do I enroll in the Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program?

To enroll, follow these steps:

Step 1: Submit an Application: Complete the online application form and submit required documents (e.g., birth certificate and previous transcripts, if applicable).

Step 2: Confirmation: Once your application is reviewed and accepted, you will receive confirmation of your enrollment.

Step 3: Course Selection: Meet with an academic adviser to choose your courses based on your grade level, academic goals and interests.

Step 4: Begin Learning: After enrollment, students can start their courses at any time and access all online resources.

Enrollment Requirements

You will need to submit the following documents for your application to be processed:

Step 1: Birth Certificate

Step 2: Proof of Texas Residency

Step 3: Unofficial Transcript

For homeschool students, please also provide a transcript and be prepared to take Credit By Exams (CBE) for grade placement.

What do I need to apply?

Step 1: The program must meet your child’s academic needs.

Step 2: Your child needs a computer with the required specs and reliable internet.

Step 3: Submit a birth certificate and proof of Texas residency.

Step 4: Your child must have achieved satisfactory performance on the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) assessments.

Tuition-Free Course Enrollment Dates

Step 1: April 5, 2027 - April 16, 2027: Grades 3-8 Reading Language Arts

Step 2: April 12, 2027 - April 23, 2027: Grade 5 Science, Grade 8 Science, Grade 8 Social Studies

Step 3: April 19, 2027 - April 30, 2027: Grades 3-8 Mathematics

Summer EOC (End of Course Exams):

Step 1: June 14, 2027 -  June 25, 2027: Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, U.S. History

Please note:

Step 1: Automatic Re-Enrollment: If you are currently enrolled in the tuition-free program, a completed re-enrollment form is required for admission to the next school year. No reapplication is necessary.

Step 2: Lottery Notification: Applications are evaluated upon submission for placement on the lottery waitlist. Applicants will be notified of their status via email.

Step 3: Tuition-Paid Programs: Enrollments for tuition-paid programs can occur at any time as long as space is available.

**Kindergarten Enrollment Requirements**

To enroll a kindergartener in the Texas Tech K-12 program, the following criteria must be met:

- **Age Requirement**: The child must be five years old on or before September 1.

- **Documents Required**:
  - Birth certificate
  - Proof of Texas residency

- **Kindergarten Acceleration (if applicable)**:
  - A score of 80% or higher on the Texas Tech K-12 Kindergarten Credit by Exam (CBE) in English language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies.
  - Additional criteria for acceleration may include:
    - A letter of recommendation from the preschool or kindergarten class the student has attended.
    - Successful completion in the first discussion-based assessment of first grade.
    - Written parental approval.

For further assistance or specific questions, contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

To transfer as a sophomore to the Texas Tech K-12 online program, the student should follow these steps:

For more detailed information or specific questions, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

A: In high performing school districts like TTU K-12, students who rank outside the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants. When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

Request a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance by emailing a request to your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. The advisor will require at least two working days for progress review.

Texas Tech K-12 High School Program - Full-Time

Texas Tech K-12 is a state-approved option for students who need or desire the flexibility of a distance education to earn their high school diploma. We offer all courses necessary to meet the requirements to complete a Texas high school graduation plan.

How do we register?

All students in grades 3-8 enrolled in the full-time, tuition-free program are automatically registered for the appropriate grade-level exams based on their enrollment status.

For students in grades 9-12 taking an End of Course-tested course (Algebra 1, Biology, English 1, English 2, and US History), Texas Tech K-12 monitors student registration upon enrollment in the 'B' semester of the course. Once enrolled, Texas Tech K-12 is required to register students for the upcoming State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness/End of Course administration. Eligibility for testing is determined by the student’s course progress.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

In addition to working towards a high school diploma, you may request a Verification of Enrollment and Student Identification (opens in new tab) cards. You may also participate in Preliminary SAT, ACT, AND SAT exams. For more information on Texas Tech High School, click on the following links:

Step 1: State and National Assessments (opens in new tab)

Step 2: Graduation Requirements (opens in new tab)
Texas Tech K-12

WHAT HAPPENS IF I CANNOT BE THERE TO TEST?

If you are ill or have an emergency, please contact your testing coordinator immediately. To ensure that you remain on schedule to graduate, participation in and successful completion of both State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness and State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness/End Of Course is necessary and is a condition of your enrollment with Texas Tech K-12. Failure to test will result in removal from the tuition-free program per our attendance policy.

Identification Cards and Verification of Enrollment (VOE)

As a full-time student, you are eligible to receive a Texas Tech K-12 student identification card and Verification of Attendance (VOE).

Verification of Attendance

If you are a full-time student who wishes to receive a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) for any purpose, including a driver’s permit, Social Security benefits or child support, avoiding truancy in your local district, or legal documentation of enrollment in a Texas Tech K-12 full-time program, you MUST meet the full-time student eligibility requirements as outlined above.

You may request a Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) Verification of Enrollment and Attendance Form or an official letter verifying enrollment and attendance from your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. Texas Tech K-12 administration may deny verification of enrollment and attendance to any student who has not maintained adequate progress to stay on grade level. Request a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance by emailing a request to your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. The advisor will require at least two working days for progress review.

If you are denied a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance, your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor will work with you to outline a progress intervention plan to meet the requirements necessary to receive a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance in the future.

answer.text:
**How Credit by Exams (CBEs) Work**

Credit by Exams (CBEs) offered by Texas Tech K-12 are designed to assess a student's mastery of a subject according to Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS). Here is how they work:

- **Purpose**: CBEs are ideal for making up a failed credit or testing out of a subject a student has already mastered.

- **Enrollment**:
  - Students can enroll in CBEs year-round, without enrollment deadlines.
  - Approval from a school counselor is recommended to ensure credit will be awarded.

- **Exam Availability**:
  - CBEs are available for six months (180 days) after purchase.
  - Students must complete the exam within this timeframe.

- **Exam Format**:
  - CBEs are available in both online and print formats.
  - Online exams require a device, browser, and ID for proctored exams.

- **Proctoring**:
  - All online CBEs require online proctoring through Proctorio, allowing students to take exams at their convenience.

- **Grading**:
  - Exams are assigned a final numerical grade.
  - No feedback is provided on the exam.

- **Refund and Transfer Policy**:
  - CBEs are non-refundable and non-transferable.
  - No extensions are allowed.

- **Passing Scores**:
  - Without prior instruction: A score of 80% or higher is required for credit.
  - With prior instruction: A score of 70% or higher is required for credit.

For more detailed information or specific questions, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.
